name: Regional memory-token use versus temporal-selection systems on DAVIS 2017
status: Frozen prospectively before SAMURAI/SAM2Long DAVIS inference; starts only after Run 159 passes its gate and completes.
question: Can predicted-region-guided memory-token merging improve DAVIS segmentation quality without choosing good or bad frames, and how does it compare with representative temporal/path-selection systems?

hypothesis.method: Soft-mask-aware local ToMe changes which nearby spatial memory keys and values are merged within each frame; it retains the native frame schedule and frozen SAM2 weights.
hypothesis.mechanism_control: The mask-aware method must be compared with generic local ToMe at the same merge budget; comparison only with native SAM2 cannot isolate the regional cue.
hypothesis.interpretation: A paired gain over native and generic ToMe supports region-guided token utilization under this setting. A matched comparison with SAMURAI/SAM2Long describes system-level competitiveness, not a pure frame-selection ablation.

dataset.name: DAVIS 2017 semi-supervised validation, 480p
dataset.prompt: All object IDs in the ground-truth indexed mask of frame 0; no later labels are read by inference.
dataset.evaluator: Pinned official DAVIS 2017 semi-supervised evaluator; score frames 1 through N-2 according to its official protocol.

shared_setup.checkpoint: SAM2.1 Hiera-Tiny (same file used in Run 159)
shared_setup.device_precision: CPU inference with frozen FP32 model weights and two PyTorch CPU threads. Preserve each pinned method's upstream arithmetic; SAM2Long stores memory features in BF16, so numerical precision is not fully matched.
shared_setup.indexed_mask_outputs: non_overlap_masks=true for all methods; packed indexed masks and first-frame prompts follow author VOS inference behavior.

author_comparators.inference: Call tools/vos_inference.py:vos_inference, the entry point used by the author's CLI when all objects are prompted in frame 0; preserve score_thresh=0 and other defaults. Instantiate a fresh predictor per video to prevent model-level Kalman state leaking across videos.
author_comparators.paper: SAMURAI: Adapting Segment Anything Model for Zero-Shot Visual Tracking with Motion-Aware Memory
author_comparators.interpretation_limit: This runs the released VOS entry point on DAVIS as our system comparison; SAMURAI's paper targets visual object tracking and its published tracking scores are not DAVIS J&F results.

author_comparators.inference: Call tools/vos_inference.py:vos_separate_inference_per_object, the entry point used by the author's CLI. Preserve documented settings: 3 pathways, IoU threshold 0.1, uncertainty 2, score threshold 0.0; instantiate a fresh predictor per video.
author_comparators.paper: SAM2Long: Enhancing SAM 2 for Long Video Segmentation with a Training-Free Memory Tree
author_comparators.settings_source: Pinned repository tools/README.md and tools/vos_inference.py parser; use the documented three-pathway command values.
author_comparators.interpretation_limit: This is the released long-video segmentation system run on DAVIS with its author VOS path, not a controlled frame-selection-only ablation.

comparisons.statistics: Treat video as the paired unit; average per-object J, F and J&F within video. Report mean and median paired differences, wins/ties/losses, 95% paired video-bootstrap intervals, paired two-sided Wilcoxon p-values, and Holm-adjusted p-values across all four contrasts.
comparisons.runtime: Report inference wall time and author pathway count separately; do not describe these as compute-matched methods.

limits: SAMURAI combines motion-aware mask selection with memory selection; it is not only a good/bad frame filter.
SAM2Long maintains multiple segmentation pathways and selects their masks/memories; it is not only frame selection.
SAM2Long's upstream implementation stores memory features in BF16 even on this CPU run; report this precision difference and do not call the comparison compute- or numerics-matched.
The additional SAMURAI/SAM2Long runs are local evaluations of pinned author implementations; do not substitute the methods' published metrics from other benchmarks or protocols.
The local ToMe arms share one schedule and key budget, so generic ToMe is the control for regional specificity.
Same Tiny checkpoint and evaluator improve comparability, but author-specific algorithms and compute remain different.
DAVIS is an external transfer benchmark but is not claimed unseen during foundation-model pretraining; it cannot replace an independent clinical cohort.
Published benchmark values remain context, not paired results.

engineering_gate.scope: Run each author VOS pipeline on the full two-object video before any val inference.
checks: Author repo revision is pinned and tracked files are clean.
Tiny checkpoint and frame-0 indexed-mask prompts match Run 159.
All expected frame PNGs are emitted at original DAVIS resolution with IDs 1 and 2.
The prompt-frame indexed output equals the supplied frame-0 mask.
Parameters remain unchanged; inference is finite and CPU FP32.
Official evaluator accepts the saved indexed masks.
